summary: Round 2 verification on the revised tech-spec. All round-1 fixes confirmed: every occurrence of the cookie-config reference now uses the correct expression `serverProperties.getReactive().getSession().getCookie()` returning `org.springframework.boot.web.server.Cookie`. New content (Decisions 6 and 7, register-auto-login regression case, TTL parameterization, technical-notes section) verified against code. Checked 28 claims; no critical or major mirages remain. Two minor observations are wording nits rather than factual mirages.

findings.claim: tech-spec line 285-286: 'extend existing tests at lines 306, 343, plus register flow'.
findings.reality: Line 306 is the *body* line of `login_success_invalidatesPreAuthSession_andSetsRememberMeTtl` (its `@Test` annotation is on 305 and method signature on 306). Line 343 is the *@Test annotation* for `login_success_noRememberMe_setsTtl24Hours` (method signature on 344). The two cited line numbers point at slightly different artifact kinds (body line vs annotation line) — both still land inside the intended tests, so the reference works in practice but is internally inconsistent.
findings.fix: Either cite both `@Test` annotation lines (305 and 343) or both signature lines (306 and 344) for consistency. Functionally not breaking — Task executor will find the correct tests either way.

findings.claim: tech-spec line 170-171 (Decision 5): 'Cookies issued before the fix (without `Max-Age`) continue to work until natural expiry or relogin'.
findings.reality: A cookie sent without `Max-Age`/`Expires` is a session cookie and is dropped by the browser at browser-close, not at any server-side 'natural expiry'. Server-side `WebSession.maxIdleTime` does evict the Mongo `sessions` document on its own schedule, but that does not extend the lifetime of the *cookie* on the client. The phrase 'natural expiry' is ambiguous — readers may interpret it as cookie-side rather than session-document-side.
findings.fix: Reword to: 'Pre-fix cookies remain valid until the browser closes (session cookie) or the user re-authenticates; the corresponding `sessions` document in Mongo continues to expire on its own `maxIdleTime` schedule. The deploy itself does not invalidate any session.' Optional — meaning is recoverable from context, but precision matters in a security-adjacent fix.
